# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** | Top talker in `conv,ip`; source of all suspicious HTTP/DNS activity |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.1.21.58` maps to this MAC |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (workgroup/NetBIOS group name `WIN11OFFICE`) | NBNS registrations from 10.1.21.58: `DESKTOP-ES9F3ML<00>`/`<20>` (unique Workstation/Server names); `WIN11OFFICE<1e>` is the Browser Election (workgroup) name, not the hostname |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller 10.1.21.2 |
| Gateway/DC | 10.1.21.2 (MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69) | Largest local conversation partner; carries LDAP/Kerberos/DRSUAPI/SMB2 traffic typical of a domain controller |

## Malware Family / Attribution

**Attribution confidence: behavioral (not signature-confirmed).** No IDS/Suricata alert export was provided alongside this pcap, so there is no signature-based naming available.

The traffic shows a classic **browser-fingerprinting gate / traffic-distribution-system (TDS)** pattern, consistent with malvertising-driven stealer/loader delivery chains:

1. **t=45.8s** — DNS lookup for `media.megafilehub4.lat` (Cloudflare-fronted, TLD `.lat`) — a fake file-download/software-hub lure domain, resolved but only TLS traffic followed (no cleartext content recoverable).
2. **t=90.3s** — DNS lookup for `whooptm.cyou` (TLD `.cyou`, another throwaway TLD typical of malvertising infrastructure).
3. **t=92.3–103.8s** — Cleartext HTTP/80 session to **whitepepper.su** (153.92.1.49). The victim made two full check-in cycles (`agent=Chrome` then `agent=Edge`) to `/api/set_agent`, each followed by a `POST .../set_agent?...&act=log` submitting a large `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body containing a **full browser/device fingerprint**: WebGL renderer/vendor, canvas fingerprint (base64 PNG), screen geometry, installed fonts, hardware concurrency, audio stack, and `navigator` properties. This is the signature behavior of a fingerprinting gate that decides whether to serve a real payload or a decoy page (anti-sandbox/anti-analyst evasion).
4. **t=122.8–126.5s** — Follow-on DNS lookups to `holiday-forever.cc` and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (both `.cc` TLD, Cloudflare-fronted), consistent with additional TDS hops or secondary gate/payload stages. All traffic to these was TLS-encrypted; no cleartext content was recoverable.

No plaintext executable download, PowerShell/mshta command, or final-stage payload was observed in the capture (all post-gate traffic is TLS-encrypted). This limits attribution to the network layer: the pattern (fake-file-hub lure → `.cyou`/`.cc`/`.lat` throwaway-TLD redirect chain → JS fingerprint-collection gate) matches known malvertising/fake-download TDS campaigns that commonly precede stealer or loader delivery (e.g., ClickFix-style or FakeUpdates-adjacent gates), but the specific stealer/loader family cannot be named with certainty from network evidence alone. I am not naming a specific malware family beyond "fingerprinting-gate/TDS commodity stealer delivery chain" because doing so would exceed what the traffic supports.

## Indicators of Compromise (grounded in capture)

**C2 / gate endpoint:**
- `153.92.1.49:80` — whitepepper.su fingerprinting gate. Evidence: cleartext HTTP GET/POST to `/api/set_agent`, tcp.stream 99/111, follow-tcp-stream shows full request/response.

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- `whitepepper.su` → 153.92.1.49 (DNS A record + Host header)
- `media.megafilehub4.lat` → 104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67 (DNS A record; TLS SNI)
- `whooptm.cyou` → 62.72.32.156 (DNS A record; TLS SNI)
- `holiday-forever.cc` → 80.97.160.24 (DNS A record; TLS SNI)
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc` → 104.21.9.36, 172.67.141.109 (DNS A record; TLS SNI)

**Malicious URLs (full, from cleartext HTTP):**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

**Correlated bot ID / token (fingerprint gate campaign ID):**
- id: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
- token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

**Transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable. All traffic past the fingerprint gate is TLS-encrypted; `--export-objects http` yielded only benign HTTP/2-labeled fragments (`%2f`) from Google/Microsoft/MSN telemetry, not from the malicious hosts. No SHA256-hashable payload was captured in cleartext.

## Benign Context (not indicators)
- 10.1.21.2 — internal domain controller (LDAP/Kerberos/SMB2/DRSUAPI traffic)
- 104.21.46.67 (`cloudflare-ech.com`) — Encrypted Client Hello SNI placeholder, largest byte conversation but real destination is obscured by ECH; not independently confirmed malicious
- Microsoft/Google/MSN telemetry and connectivity domains (`msftconnecttest.com`, `clients*.google.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `*.msn.com`, `office.com`, `windows.com`, etc.) — normal Windows 11/Office/Edge background traffic
- SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR/NBNS broadcast noise — normal LAN discovery traffic

## Summary

Windows workstation **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (10.1.21.58, MAC 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2), logged in as domain user **gwyatt**, visited a fake file-download lure (`media.megafilehub4.lat`) and was redirected through `whooptm.cyou` into a JavaScript browser-fingerprinting gate at **whitepepper.su** (153.92.1.49:80), which collected a detailed device/browser fingerprint (WebGL, canvas, fonts, hardware) under a tracked bot ID/token before likely branching to a payload stage. All traffic beyond the fingerprint gate (`holiday-forever.cc`, `communicationfirewall-security.cc`) was TLS-encrypted, so no final payload, executable, or hash could be extracted from this capture; the malware family delivered after the gate cannot be confirmed from network evidence alone and attribution here is limited to behavioral (TDS/fingerprint-gate) classification.
